insights.title: Nevis leads the ranking
insights.text: Nevis ranks first with £30.3m in total raised, 15.2x the £2.0m recorded by the company in last place.

insights.title: Value is concentrated at the top
insights.text: The top 10 companies hold 33% of the combined total raised (£205.4m), 3.3x what an even split would give them.

insights.title: A few large rounds pull the average up
insights.text: The median company has £4.1m, against an average of £6.2m. The gap shows that a small number of companies account for an outsized share.

insights.title: London dominates by region
insights.text: London accounts for 78 of the 100 companies (78%) and 81% of the combined total raised.

insights.title: South West punches above its weight
insights.text: The 5 companies in South West (by region) average £10.0m, compared with £6.2m across the full list.

insights.title: Every company shares the same stage
insights.text: All 100 companies in the list share the same stage: Seed.

insights.title: 25-49 punches above its weight
insights.text: The 10 companies in 25-49 (by employees) average £9.7m, compared with £6.2m across the full list.

insights.title: Application software is the most common sub-sector
insights.text: 98 of the 100 UK fintech companies are classed as Application software, followed by Data provision and analysis (35).

insights.title: Risk and compliance attracts the most per company
insights.text: Among sub-sectors with at least 5 companies, Risk and compliance has the highest average at £7.9m.

copy.title: Top 100 UK Fintech Companies in 2026
copy.metaDescription: The top 100 UK Fintech companies ranked by total raised, led by Nevis. Full ranking, key statistics and insights for 2026.
intro: This ranking lists the top 100 UK Fintech companies by total raised. Every figure on this page is calculated directly from the underlying dataset.
Below you will find the headline numbers, how the companies break down by region, stage and employees, and the full ranking table.

sections.heading: The top UK Fintech companies by total raised
paragraphs: Nevis (£30.3m), Januus.io (£27.9m) and Adfin (£24.2m) make up the top three. Together the ten highest-ranked companies account for £205.4m, or 33% of the £622.3m recorded across the full list.
Reaching the ranking is itself a marker of scale: the company in last place has £2.0m in total raised.

sections.heading: How total raised is distributed across UK Fintech
paragraphs: The median company has £4.1m in total raised, while the average is £6.2m. Because the average sits well above the median, a small group of large companies is lifting the overall figures.
The most common band is £2.5m–£5.0m, which covers 38 companies. Overall, total raised is moderately concentrated (Gini coefficient 0.41).

sections.heading: UK Fintech companies by region
paragraphs: The largest group by region is London, with 78 companies (78%), followed by North West with 6. Together this group accounts for 81% of the combined total raised, led by Nevis.

sections.heading: UK Fintech companies by stage
paragraphs: Every company in the ranking shares the same stage: Seed. That makes this list a like-for-like comparison of UK Fintech companies at the same point.

sections.heading: UK Fintech companies by employees
paragraphs: The largest group by employees is 10-24, with 49 companies (49%), followed by 5-9 with 23. Together this group accounts for 46% of the combined total raised, led by TreeCard.

sections.heading: The most common UK Fintech sub-sectors
paragraphs: Companies can sit in more than one sub-sector. The most frequent are Application software (98), Data provision and analysis (35), Wealth, asset and investment management (27) and Budgeting and financial management (24).

sections.heading: What the data tells us about UK Fintech
paragraphs: Taken together, total raised across the top UK Fintech companies is moderately concentrated and the group is fairly uniform: 78% share the same region (London) and 100% share the same stage (Seed). For investors, partners and analysts, the ranking offers a quick way to identify the most established names in the sector and where activity is clustered.
